1	---
2	title: "Graphics in a vertical version"
3	description: How Make Vertical Version re-sizes and re-lays your graphics for a tall or square canvas, which older template copies it updates, and which modules it names for you to check.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) has to turn a wide layout into a tall or square one, and graphics can lay themselves out again where footage can't. This page says what happens to each graphic, and which ones you might want to look at afterwards.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
12	  tools="make_vertical_version"
13	/>
14	
15	## Canvas-sized graphics
16	
17	A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, each side, is re-sized to the new canvas, so its [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/), the code that draws it, lays it out again on the new frame. This is usually a full-frame lower third or title card. A 1920 × 1080 graphic on a 1920 × 1080 canvas becomes 1080 × 1920 for 9:16.
18	
19	Its position shrinks and stretches with the two sides of the canvas, and so do the positions its [actions](/graphics/animate-properties/) move it to. Its scale stays as it was, because the graphic is the canvas's size again.
20	
21	This is the one change of canvas that changes a graphic's size. Everywhere else, [Width and Height](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height) stay as you set them.
22	
23	## Graphics of any other size
24	
25	Any other graphic is kept as placed and rescaled from the old canvas, like a title. That includes a graphic with the same area as the canvas but another shape, such as 1080 × 1920 on a 1920 × 1080 canvas.
26	
27	## Templates measured by the short side
28	
29	Every [bundled template](/graphics/templates/) measures itself by the short side of the size it draws at, so it fits a tall frame. Older copies of these six measured by the height instead:
30	
31	- Lower third
32	- Title card
33	- Callout
34	- Bar chart
35	- Counter
36	- Kinetic type
37	
38	The current six draw exactly as those older copies did on a landscape or square canvas.
39	
40	## Older template copies
41	
42	A project can hold an older copy of one of those six, inserted before they measured by the short side. Frame Job looks at every module a clip draws, on the timeline and inside nests, and recognises these by their text, never their name. A copy you renamed `intro` is still found.
43	
44	What happens next depends on **Make a copy** in the Make Vertical Version sheet:
45	
46	| **Make a copy** | What happens |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| Ticked | The copy that opens has each older module rewritten with the current template. Your earlier text is kept as the module's previous version, so [File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…](/graphics/manage-graphics/) brings it back. The project you started from never changes. |
49	| Unticked | Nothing is rewritten, and the summary names each module. |
50	
51	## Your own modules
52	
53	A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height, with `ctx.height / 1080` in its text, is named in the summary, because it may not fit the narrow frame. This applies with or without **Make a copy**, and the module is never rewritten.
54	
55	A template you've edited counts as your own, since its text no longer matches any template Frame Job shipped.
56	
57	To fix one of these, measure by the short side instead:
58	
59	```js
60	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
61	```
62	
63	On a landscape canvas that's the same number as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a tall canvas drawing the graphic 1.78 times too big. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
64	
65	## What the summary says
66	
67	The sheet's summary reports all of this before you choose **Make**, and it stays accurate as you change the sheet. The exception is while it says it will find faces, people and shot changes first: that summary lists none of this.
68	
69	| The summary says | What it means |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| "Re-sizes 2 graphics to the new canvas." | That many canvas-sized graphics are being re-sized. |
72	| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | That many older template copies are rewritten in the copy. |
73	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." | You've unticked **Make a copy**. Tick it to update the module. |
74	| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it sizes itself by the canvas's height, so it may not fit the narrow frame." | Check this graphic on the new canvas. |
75	
76	## With an agent
77	
78	`make_vertical_version` reports the same things in `graphics` when it finishes: how many graphics it re-sized, the modules it updated, and each module it left as it is, with the reason. See [Tools: framing and vertical](/mcp/tools-framing/).
79

2	title: "Show video inside a graphic"
3	description: "Use a graphic as a matte so your footage plays through the shape it draws, and animate that shape like any other graphic."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A graphic can't read a video's pixels, but it can shape one. Make the graphic's track a matte and the video behind it shows only where the graphic draws, or, inverted, only where it doesn't.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Track ▸ Matte"
13	  tools={['set_track']}
14	/>
15	
16	## Show video inside a graphic
17	
18	<Steps>
19	
20	1. Put the video on a track, and the graphic on the track directly above it. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
21	
22	2. Line the graphic clip up with the stretch of video you want cut. Where the matte track has no clip, the video shows uncut.
23	
24	3. Select the graphic clip.
25	
26	4. Choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Alpha**.
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	The graphic itself is no longer drawn. What it shows now decides where the video can be seen. To go back, choose **Track ▸ Matte ▸ Off**.
31	
32	## Choose a mode
33	
34	| Mode | The video shows where the graphic is |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| **Alpha** | Opaque |
37	| **Inverted Alpha** | Transparent |
38	| **Luma** | Bright |
39	| **Inverted Luma** | Dark |
40	
41	**Off** makes it an ordinary track again.
42	
43	## Write a module for a matte
44	
45	A matte module is written and called exactly like any other, and the cut follows each frame as it animates. Fill the window in white so it works in every mode.
46	
47	This one opens a rounded window with a spring:
48	
49	```js
50	export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
51	export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };
52	
53	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
54	  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
55	  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
56	  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
57	  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
58	    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
59	}
60	```
61	
62	Its **radius** property appears on the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/) as usual, and you can [animate it](/graphics/animate-properties/). See [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/).
63	
64	## What the clip's settings still do
65	
66	The graphic clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window, so you can move or fade it with the same controls as any clip.
67	
68	Its blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. They're kept, and they apply again if the track stops being a matte.
69	
70	The video's own drop shadow follows the cut-out shape.
71	
72	## Good to know
73	
74	Only the track directly behind the matte is cut, so tracks further back and the canvas show through the hole. [Matte tracks](/canvas/matte-tracks/) has the whole story, including what happens with two matte tracks in a row and how a matte looks on the timeline.
75	
76	## With an agent
77	
78	`set_track` sets a track's `matte` to `alpha`, `alpha_inverted`, `luma` or `luma_inverted`, and `none` turns it off. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#track-mattes).
79

2	title: Graphics with an agent
3	description: Let an agent write a graphic module, look at its frames, place it on the timeline and check the result, and see what undo covers.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An agent is an AI tool that works in Frame Job for you, such as Claude Code connected over MCP, or the [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/). You describe the graphic you want, and it can make it from start to finish: read the API, write the [module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#modules) that draws it, look at it, place it, change it and check the finished frame. This page follows that loop and says what undo covers along the way.
10	
11	Each tool's arguments are on [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).
12	
13	<AtAGlance
14	  menu={['Help ▸ Graphics Reference', 'Insert ▸ Graphic…']}
15	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic']}
16	  tools={[
17	    'graphic_reference',
18	    'write_graphic',
19	    'render_graphic',
20	    'get_graphic',
21	    'list_graphics',
22	    'insert_graphic',
23	    'add_graphic_clip',
24	    'set_graphic',
25	    'import_graphic_font',
26	    'import_graphic_asset',
27	    'add_action',
28	    'set_action_end',
29	    'render_frame',
30	  ]}
31	  needs="A client connected over MCP, or the Assistant tab with your Anthropic key."
32	/>
33	
34	## The loop
35	
36	<Steps>
37	
38	1. **Read the API.** `graphic_reference` returns it. An agent reads it once, before writing a graphic.
39	
40	2. **Write the module.** `write_graphic` saves the module, compiles it and says whether that worked. Fix the source and write again until it compiles.
41	
42	3. **Look at it.** `render_graphic` draws frames on a contact sheet with no clip on the timeline.
43	
44	4. **Add what it draws with.** `import_graphic_font` adds a font and `import_graphic_asset` adds a picture. The reply to a font import gives the exact family names to write in `font-family`, and the reply to a picture import gives the name to pass to `asset()`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
45	
46	5. **Place it and change it.** `add_graphic_clip` places a clip and `set_graphic` changes it. To animate a property, `add_action` adds an action and `set_action_end` says what the property ends at. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
47	
48	6. **Check the result.** `render_frame` shows a frame of the finished timeline.
49	
50	</Steps>
51	
52	## Read the API
53	
54	`graphic_reference` returns the whole graphics API as Markdown: the module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, limits and idioms. It's the same file **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** opens, and an agent only needs to read it once.
55	
56	No project needs to be open. If the call names a project, it must be one that's open.
57	
58	## Write a module
59	
60	`write_graphic` saves `graphics/<name>.js` in the project, compiles that exact text and reports the result. It creates the `graphics` folder the first time, and the file is written in one go, so nothing ever reads half of it.
61	
62	A module's name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`. It starts with a letter or a digit and is at most 63 characters.
63	
64	The reply says whether the module compiled, what its `meta` and `schema` are, which clips it draws, which earlier versions are kept, and each problem with its line and column. A module that doesn't compile is still a normal reply, not a failed call, so the agent reads where it went wrong and writes again. When a module does compile, any problems listed are warnings from its top level, such as an `asset()` call there that names a file the folder doesn't hold.
65	
66	Clips already drawn by the module redraw at once. The write can't be undone, but the text it replaced is kept: see [Undo rules](#undo-rules).
67	
68	[Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) has the shape of the file itself.
69	
70	## A contact sheet
71	
72	`render_graphic` draws a module without placing a clip: up to 16 frames on one PNG, with each frame's number printed under it. It's how an agent looks at a graphic before committing it to the timeline. There's no inspector control for it, because a person watches the preview instead.
73	
74	| Choice | What it does | Default |
75	| --- | --- | --- |
76	| Frames | Which frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them in order, or a single frame | Frame 0 |
77	| Properties | The values to draw with. A property left out draws with the schema's default. | The schema's defaults |
78	| Size | The width and height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas |
79	| Widest sheet | How wide the PNG may be, 64 to 8192 pixels | 2048 |
80	| Background | What the sheet is painted on: transparent, a checker, or a hex colour (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`) | Transparent |
81	| Where it's written | A path whose folder already exists | A temporary file |
82	
83	The frames sit on a near-square grid. Frames are scaled down to fit the sheet's width, never up, and the gaps and frame numbers stay at full size. Raise the widest sheet to see frames larger.
84	
85	Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it, at the project's frame rate and with a length from the module's `meta`, else 5 seconds. A frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `ctx.progress` at 1, as a longer clip would draw it.
86	
87	A frame that fails is drawn as its [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card), and the reply adds a sentence naming the frame and the problem, with its line and column when the engine has them. A frame that warns gets a sentence too.
88	
89	A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames in all, which is two frames at 8192 × 8192 or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call fails before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.
90	
91	:::note
92	The sheet gives each frame the 2 seconds an export does, not the preview's 250 ms. A frame that draws here can still run over its [time budget](/graphics/write-a-module/#the-time-budget) in the preview.
93	:::
94	
95	## One frame's SVG
96	
97	Asked for `svg` instead of the default `png`, `render_graphic` returns one frame's SVG text, its problems and the `ctx` it was drawn with. Use it to read the markup a frame produced.
98	
99	It takes one frame and writes no file, so naming several frames, a background, a widest sheet or a path is an error. If the frame fails, the reply says so and holds no SVG.
100	
101	## List and insert
102	
103	`list_graphics` lists what the Insert Graphic sheet shows, in the sheet's order. **This Project** comes first when the project holds a module, listing every module whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, with **Other** last.
104	
105	Each entry has its name, title, description and category, says whether it's a template or a project module, and says whether it compiles. The title is the module's `meta.name`, else its file name made into a title. Two project modules with the same title are shown as "title — name".
106	
107	`insert_graphic` is the sheet's **Insert**. It places a clip at the playhead, on the front track when it fits there and otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's own length and size. That's one undo step. With a nest open, the clip lands inside it.
108	
109	- A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name, such as `lower-third` then `lower-third-2`. The copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert removes the clip and leaves the file. The reply names the module the clip is drawn by.
110	- A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
111	- A module that doesn't compile places nothing, and the call fails with its first error. A template's copy stays in the folder.
112	
113	See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
114	
115	## Place a clip
116	
117	`add_graphic_clip` places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on the track and at the time the agent chooses. It can also place the clip inside a nest. Use `insert_graphic` when the playhead is the right place.
118	
119	| Choice | Default | Limit |
120	| --- | --- | --- |
121	| Length | The module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the project's rate, else 5 seconds | At least one frame |
122	| Width and height | The module's `meta` size, else the canvas | 1 to 8192 pixels each |
123	| Properties | The schema's defaults | At most 64 |
124	
125	Each property is checked against the module's schema when the clip is placed. A key the schema lacks, a value of the wrong type, a number out of range or an option that isn't listed stops the call, and the error names the property. Colours are stored as lowercase hex.
126	
127	Frame Job won't place the clip when:
128	
129	- The module isn't in the folder. The error says what the folder holds.
130	- The module doesn't compile. The error gives its first problem.
131	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The error names the key.
132	- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given. The error names the canvas.
133	- The clip would overlap another one on the track, as for any clip.
134	
135	## Change a clip
136	
137	`set_graphic` changes what one or more graphic clips are drawn from: another module, the size, the graphic's own length or the properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/).
138	
139	- **Properties** merge key by key, and a clip stores at most 64. Clearing a property removes it. A property that an action on the clip animates is set to the module's default instead, so the animation keeps its start.
140	- **Length** snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Clearing it is **Follow Clip**. See [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
141	- **In** can't be set here. It changes only when you trim or split the clip.
142	
143	These are the clip's base values. To animate one, add an action and set its end.
144	
145	Clips drawn by two different modules can't take a property change together, unless the same call names one module for them all, and a clip that isn't a graphic is an error. A call that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes re-sending a colour in another spelling.
146	
147	## Read a module or the folder
148	
149	`get_graphic` with a name reads one module: its source, revision, path, whether it compiles, its `meta`, `schema` and problems, the clips it draws, and its kept versions, newest first. The **Source** section shows you the file, revision and problems.
150	
151	With no name it reads the folder:
152	
153	- The folder's path, given even before the folder exists. The first write creates it.
154	- Every module with its revision, whether it compiles and the clips it draws.
155	- The font families and pictures the project's graphics can use.
156	- Anything the folder's scan skipped or couldn't watch, in its own sentences.
157	- Every name with kept versions, deleted modules included.
158	
159	## File tools
160	
161	An agent can also edit the graphics folder with its own file tools, and Frame Job sees the change within a moment.
162	
163	| What | Where |
164	| --- | --- |
165	| Modules | `graphics/<name>.js` |
166	| Fonts | `graphics/fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
167	| Pictures | `graphics/assets/` |
168	
169	`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept versions, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference and its types.
170	
171	A module saved a moment ago can read as not compiling, with one problem saying Frame Job hasn't compiled it yet. Ask again.
172	
173	In a project that hasn't been saved, the folder is a temporary one. It moves when the project is saved, so ask `get_graphic` for the path again afterwards.
174	
175	See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up and how many files are watched.
176	
177	## Undo rules
178	
179	The files in `graphics/` live beside the project, not in its undo history. Changes to the clips on the timeline are ordinary undo steps.
180	
181	| Action | Undo step? | Marks the project edited? |
182	| --- | --- | --- |
183	| `write_graphic`, `restore_graphic`, `delete_graphic` | No | No |
184	| `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset` | No | No |
185	| `add_graphic_clip`, `insert_graphic`, `set_graphic` | Yes | Yes |
186	| `rename_graphic` | Yes, for the clips that follow the new name, as one step | Only through the clips |
187	
188	Undoing a rename moves the file back along with the clips, and redo moves it forward again. With no clips drawn by the module, a rename makes no undo step. `import_graphic` can't be undone either, and `export_graphic` edits nothing, so it has no undo step.
189	
190	Because a file write can't be undone, Frame Job keeps the last 10 texts each module replaced, and `restore_graphic` brings one back. A deleted module's text is kept the same way. See [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
191	
192	## Graphics in render frame
193	
194	`render_frame` shows a frame of the timeline as an export would draw it. When a graphic in that frame failed or warned, the reply has a sentence naming the graphic, its frame and the problem. A graphic that failed draws its error card in the picture. See [Check the picture: render_frame](/mcp/render-frame/).
195	
196	## The Assistant
197	
198	The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) uses these same tools, so you can ask it in the inspector to write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics. It already knows a graphic is a module and where to read what a module can draw, so plain words are enough. It needs your [Anthropic key](/assistant/set-up/).
199	
200	It asks before `export_graphic`, because that writes a package where the model chose and replaces any file already there. Nothing is written until you choose **Allow**. Importing a package doesn't ask, because it only writes inside the project's `graphics/`.
201

1	---
2	title: "The module API"
3	description: "The helpers every graphic module can call, what each one takes and returns, and where to open the full graphics reference."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A graphic is drawn by a small JavaScript module, and every module can call a standard library of helpers for animating values, blending colours, measuring text and following paths. This page is for you if you're writing or changing a module: it names each helper with what it's for, and points you to the full reference. You don't need it to use a graphic.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Help ▸ Graphics Reference"
12	  where="API.md and API.d.ts in a project's graphics folder"
13	  tools="graphic_reference"
14	/>
15	
16	All of these are already there when your module runs, so there's nothing to import. The examples use the arguments of `render(frame, props, ctx)`: `frame` is the frame being drawn, `props` holds the values set in the inspector, and `ctx` holds the size, frame rate and progress. [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/) explains them.
17	
18	## The graphics reference
19	
20	Choose **Help ▸ Graphics Reference** to open the whole API in your default Markdown app, with or without a project open. It covers a module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, the limits and the worked examples. The menu item is dimmed only if the reference file is missing from the app.
21	
22	Frame Job also keeps two files beside your modules once a project has a graphics folder:
23	
24	| File | What it is |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| `API.md` | The same reference. |
27	| `API.d.ts` | Type definitions for the whole API, for an editor or an agent working in the folder. |
28	
29	Frame Job doesn't make a graphics folder only to hold them. Don't edit them, because Frame Job puts its own text back over any change.
30	
31	An agent reads the same reference with `graphic_reference`, which needs no project open. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
32	
33	## Find a helper
34	
35	| To | Use |
36	| --- | --- |
37	| Write the root `<svg>` element | [`svg`](#svg) |
38	| Move a number from one value to another | [`interpolate`](#interpolate) |
39	| Shape that movement | [`Easing`](#easing) |
40	| Move with bounce and settle | [`spring`](#spring) |
41	| Blend colours | [`interpolateColors`](#interpolatecolors) |
42	| Get a repeatable random number | [`random`](#random) |
43	| Add smooth, organic drift | [`noise2D` and `noise3D`](#noise) |
44	| Measure a path, follow it, or draw it on | [`getLength`, `getPointAtLength` and `evolvePath`](#path-helpers) |
45	| Measure text | [`measureText`](#measuretext) |
46	| Break text into lines | [`wrapText`](#wraptext) |
47	| Size text to a width | [`fitText`](#fittext) |
48	| Write lines of text as markup | [`textLines`](#textlines) |
49	| Make a prop safe to put in markup | [`escapeXml`](#escapexml) |
50	| Group a number's thousands | [`formatNumber`](#formatnumber) |
51	| Draw a picture from the project | [`asset`](#asset) |
52	
53	## Start the frame
54	
55	### `svg()`
56	
57	`svg(ctx, body, {background})` writes the root element with the right `width`, `height` and `viewBox`, around whatever markup you pass as `body`.
58	
59	```js
60	const plain = svg(ctx, `<circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="#fff"/>`);
61	const onBlack = svg(ctx, "", { background: "#000000" });
62	```
63	
64	`background` is optional and paints the whole frame in a colour. Leave it out and the frame stays clear behind what you draw. `body` goes in exactly as you wrote it, so a prop inside it needs [`escapeXml`](#escapexml).
65	
66	## Animate values
67	
68	### `interpolate()`
69	
70	`interpolate(value, input, output, options)` maps a value through matching ranges. It's the helper most animation starts from.
71	
72	```js
73	const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 400], { clamp: true });
74	const pulse = interpolate(frame, [0, 15, 30], [1, 1.2, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutSine });
75	```
76	
77	`input` and `output` need two or more points each, and the same number of them, or the helper throws. Keep `input` ascending.
78	
79	| Option | What it does | Default |
80	| --- | --- | --- |
81	| `easing` | A curve from [`Easing`](#easing), applied inside each pair of points. | Straight line |
82	| `clamp` | With `true`, the result stops at the first and last `output` values. | `false` |
83	| `extrapolateLeft` | What happens before the first `input` point: `"extend"`, `"clamp"` or `"identity"`. | `"extend"`, or `"clamp"` when `clamp` is `true` |
84	| `extrapolateRight` | The same after the last `input` point. | `"extend"`, or `"clamp"` when `clamp` is `true` |
85	
86	Outside `input`, `"extend"` carries on along the end segment, so `interpolate(40, [0, 30], [0, 400])` gives about 533. `"identity"` returns `value` unchanged. Either `extrapolate` option wins over `clamp` on its own side.
87	
88	### `Easing`
89	
90	`Easing` holds ready-made curves to pass to `interpolate`. You can also call one directly: each takes `t` from 0 to 1 and is exact at 0 and 1.
91	
92	- `Easing.linear`
93	- `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, which makes a curve of your own
94	- `in`, `out` and `inOut` of `quad`, `cubic`, `quart`, `expo`, `sine`, `back` and `elastic`, spelled `Easing.inQuad`, `Easing.outCubic`, `Easing.inOutBack` and so on
95	
96	```js
97	const eased = Easing.outCubic(0.5);
98	const custom = Easing.bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)(0.5);
99	const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [300, 0], { easing: Easing.outBack, clamp: true });
100	```
101	
102	The `back` and `elastic` curves go past the end of their range on the way. `clamp` doesn't stop that, because it only holds the value once `input` runs out.
103	
104	### `spring()`
105	
106	`spring()` gives a physical spring from one value to another.
107	
108	```js
109	const scale = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
110	const late = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, stiffness: 180, from: 0.5, to: 1 });
111	```
112	
113	| Option | What it does | Default |
114	| --- | --- | --- |
115	| `frame` | The frame to read the spring at. | Needed |
116	| `fps` | The frame rate. Pass `ctx.fps`. | Needed |
117	| `stiffness` | How hard the spring pulls towards `to`. | 100 |
118	| `damping` | How quickly the movement dies away. | 10 |
119	| `mass` | How heavy the thing moving is. | 1 |
120	| `from` | Where it starts. | 0 |
121	| `to` | Where it settles. | 1 |
122	
123	A spring starts at frame 0 and sits at `from` before that, so `frame - 12` starts it 12 frames late. It overshoots unless it's damped: on the defaults it reaches about 1.16 on its way to 1, and with the default stiffness and mass a `damping` of 20 or more stops the overshoot. The same frame always gives the same value.
124	
125	### `interpolateColors()`
126	
127	`interpolateColors(value, input, colors)` blends colours in OKLab, a colour space built so that a blend looks even. It returns `#rrggbb`, or `#rrggbbaa` when any of the colours isn't fully opaque.
128	
129	```js
130	const fill = interpolateColors(frame, [0, 60], ["#ff5a36", "#3666ff"]);
131	const glass = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)", "#ffffff"]);
132	const sky = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["hsl(200, 80%, 30%)", "skyblue"]);
133	```
134	
135	`input` works as it does in `interpolate`, with two or more points and one colour for each. Outside `input` the result always holds at the end colours.
136	
137	It takes the same colours a `color` prop takes:
138	
139	| Form | Notes |
140	| --- | --- |
141	| `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa` | |
142	| `rgb()`, `rgba()` | Channels 0 to 255 or a percentage, alpha 0 to 1 or a percentage. |
143	| `hsl()`, `hsla()` | Hue in degrees, saturation and lightness as percentages. |
144	| A name | Any of the 147 CSS colour names, or `transparent`. |
145	
146	A value out of range, such as `rgb(300, 0, 0)`, throws rather than being clamped.
147	
148	## Add variation
149	
150	### `random()`
151	
152	`random(seed)` returns a number from 0 up to, but not including, 1. It depends only on the seed, which is a number or a string, so the same seed gives the same number on every frame and in every export.
153	
154	```js
155	const jitter = random(`dot-${frame}`) * 10;
156	const hue = Math.floor(random(42) * 360);
157	```
158	
159	Put the frame in the seed for a value that changes, as `jitter` does, and leave it out for one that stays. The seed is read as text, so `42` and `"42"` give the same number.
160	
161	`Math.random` isn't available in a graphic. Calling it throws "Math.random is not available; use random(seed)".
162	
163	### Noise
164	
165	`noise2D(seed, x, y)` and `noise3D(seed, x, y, z)` give simplex noise for organic motion: a value between −1 and 1 that changes smoothly as its inputs do. The seed works as it does for `random`.
166	
167	```js
168	const drift = noise2D("wave", frame / 60, 0) * 40;
169	const wobble = noise3D(7, 0.5, 0.5, ctx.time) * 20;
170	```
171	
172	For smooth drift, use `noise3D` with time as the third axis.
173	
174	## Path helpers
175	
176	These three take `d`, ordinary SVG path data. Every command works, in its absolute and relative forms: `M L H V C S Q T A Z`.
177	
178	| Helper | What it returns |
179	| --- | --- |
180	| `getLength(d)` | The path's length. Curves and arcs are measured in short straight pieces, so the answer can be a few hundredths of a percent short. |
181	| `getPointAtLength(d, length)` | `{x, y, angle}`: the point that far along, and the way the path is heading there in degrees, ready for `rotate()`. A `length` outside the path stops at its nearest end. |
182	| `evolvePath(progress, d)` | `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress` from 0 to 1. Put both on the `<path>` and it's drawn from its start up to that fraction. |
183	
184	```js
185	const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
186	const total = getLength(d);
187	const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
188	const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
189	const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
190	  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
191	  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
192	```
193	
194	`evolvePath` keeps `progress` between 0 and 1, and a closed outline closes at 1. A path of several pieces, with more than one `M`, draws them all at once, each from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1. To draw pieces one after another, give each its own `<path>`.
195	
196	A path has to start with a move, `M` or `m`. One that can't be read throws, naming where reading stopped, for example `getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"`. It's never a silent zero, though an empty `d` measures 0. A number too large to do arithmetic with, such as `1e999`, throws the same error, so you never get `Infinity` or `NaN` back.
197	
198	Frame Job remembers the paths a graphic measures, so the same `d` costs almost nothing on later calls and frames. It holds up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and measured pieces between them, where a curve is 64 pieces. Past either limit it forgets them all and measures again when asked. With paths that large, take every length and point you need from one before turning to the next.
199	
200	## Work with text
201	
202	The text helpers measure with the same fonts the graphic draws with: the ones bundled with Frame Job and any in the project, never the system's. [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) lists them.
203	
204	### `measureText()`
205	
206	`measureText(text, font)` measures text. `font` is an object, and all four text helpers read it the same way:
207	
208	| Key | What it does | Default |
209	| --- | --- | --- |
210	| `family` | The font family. | `"Montserrat"` |
211	| `size` | The size in pixels, above 0. | 16 |
212	| `weight` | The weight, 1 to 1000. | 400 |
213	| `style` | `"normal"`, `"italic"` or `"oblique"`. | `"normal"` |
214	| `letterSpacing` | Extra space between letters. | 0 |
215	| `xmlSpace` | `"default"` collapses runs of spaces, as SVG draws them. `"preserve"` counts them, as `xml:space="preserve"` draws them. | `"default"` |
216	
217	It returns `{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`. `width` is the advance, which is where the next word would start. `inkX` and `inkWidth` describe the glyphs actually drawn.
218	
219	```js
220	const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
221	const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
222	const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
223	```
224	
225	A family that isn't installed throws, naming the families that are. Any `xmlSpace` other than those two throws too. Text that's only spaces measures zero either way.
226	
227	### `wrapText()`
228	
229	`wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)` breaks text into lines that each fit `maxWidth`, and returns them as a list. A word longer than the width breaks by characters.
230	
231	```js
232	const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
233	  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
234	```
235	
236	Line breaks in the text count as spaces, so split on them first if you want to keep them.
237	
238	### `fitText()`
239	
240	`fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min, max})` returns the largest whole font size at which the text fits on one line. `min` defaults to 8 and `max` to 400, and the `size` in `font` is ignored.
241	
242	```js
243	const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
244	```
245	
246	It never goes outside `min` and `max`, so text too long to fit at `min` still comes back as `min` and runs over. Empty text returns `max`.
247	
248	### `textLines()`
249	
250	`textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})` writes a `<text>` element with one `<tspan>` per line.
251	
252	```js
253	const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
254	const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
255	  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
256	```
257	
258	| Option | What it does | Default |
259	| --- | --- | --- |
260	| `x`, `y` | Where the first line goes. | 0 |
261	| `lineHeight` | The distance between lines. | 1.2 × the size |
262	| `anchor` | `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`. | `"start"` |
263	| `fill` | The text colour. | Not written |
264	| `font` | The same `font` object as `measureText`. | |
265	
266	It does the fiddly parts for you. It quotes the family, leaving a generic such as `sans-serif` bare as it has to be. It escapes each line, so don't pass lines through `escapeXml` first. It also writes `font-style`, `letter-spacing` and `xml:space` to match the font `wrapText` broke the lines with, so what's drawn is what was measured.
267	
268	## Prepare values
269	
270	### `escapeXml()`
271	
272	`escapeXml(s)` escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`, so a prop is safe to write into markup. Put every prop you write into markup through it. Without it, a title like "Tom & Jerry" stops the frame with an error that starts "the SVG did not parse".
273	
274	```js
275	const safe = escapeXml("Tom & Jerry <live>");
276	```
277	
278	The exception is text you pass to [`textLines`](#textlines), which escapes it already. Escaping twice puts `&` on screen.
279	
280	### `formatNumber()`
281	
282	`formatNumber(n, {decimals, separator})` groups thousands, because a graphic has no `Intl`. `decimals` defaults to 0 and `separator` to a comma.
283	
284	```js
285	const label = formatNumber(1234567.891, { decimals: 2 });
286	const plain = formatNumber(Math.round(interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, 5000], { clamp: true })));
287	```
288	
289	`label` here is `1,234,567.89`. The number is rounded to `decimals`, a minus sign is kept, and `NaN` or `Infinity` comes back as that word.
290	
291	## Draw a picture
292	
293	### `asset()`
294	
295	`asset(name)` returns the `href` of a file in the project's `graphics/assets/` folder, for an `<image>` element.
296	
297	```js
298	const logo = `<image href="${asset("logo.png")}" x="40" y="40" width="200" height="200"/>`;
299	```
300	
301	A name that isn't in the folder gives a warning naming the files that are, and the image doesn't draw. [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) covers adding pictures and how they're named.
302	
303	## Idioms
304	
305	The reference ends with six complete modules, each showing a common move. You can copy any of them into a graphic and it works as written. Find them under **Idioms** in **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.
306	
307	| Idiom | What it shows | The key line |
308	| --- | --- | --- |
309	| A slide-in | Text sliding in with `interpolate` and `Easing`. | `interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [-ctx.width / 2, ctx.width / 2], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true })` |
310	| A staggered list | Rows springing in one after another. | `spring({ frame: frame - i * 6, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 })` |
311	| A counter | A number counting up. | `formatNumber(Math.round(value)) + props.suffix` |
312	| Fit and wrap a title | A title sized and wrapped to the frame. | `fitText(props.title, maxWidth * 2, base, { min: 48, max: 220 })`, then `wrapText` and `textLines` |
313	| A draw-on stroke | A line drawing itself. | `evolvePath(drawn, d)` |
314	| Follow a path | An arrowhead following a curve. | `getPointAtLength(d, getLength(d) * drawn)`, then `rotate(${tip.angle})` |
315	
316	All six work out their positions and sizes from `ctx`, so the same module draws at any size. The exception is the `min` and `max` in Fit and wrap a title, which are fixed sizes. A slide-in and A staggered list scale everything by this unit, which also keeps a portrait canvas from drawing too big:
317	
318	```js
319	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
320	```
321	
322	## Good to know
323	
324	- A helper that throws stops that frame, and the clip draws the [error card](/graphics/edit-a-module/#the-error-card) in place of the graphic. The Source section of [the Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/) shows what the clip's first frame reported, with its line and column.
325	- `import` isn't available. A module that tries it stops with an error ending "imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global".

17	## Try your first module
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Save the example under [The module](#the-module) as `lower-third.js`, anywhere you like.
22	
23	2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**, then **From File…**, and pick the file. Frame Job copies it into the project's `graphics` folder and places a clip at the playhead.
24	
25	3. Select the clip and open **Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source**. Choose **Open in Editor**, change something and save. The clip redraws. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	A file name is lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starts with a letter or a digit, and is at most 63 characters before `.js`. **From File…** makes a valid name from whatever you pick. If the module doesn't compile, the copy stays in the folder and no clip is placed.
30	
31	## The module
32	
33	A module is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`.
34	
35	```js
36	export const meta = {
37	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
38	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
39	};
40	
41	export const schema = {
42	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
43	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
44	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
45	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
46	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
47	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
48	};
49	
50	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
51	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
52	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
53	    { clamp: true });
54	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
55	  return svg(ctx, `
56	    <g opacity="${fade}">
57	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
58	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
59	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
60	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
61	    </g>`);
62	}
63	```
64	
65	| Export | Required | What it is |
66	| --- | --- | --- |
67	| `render(frame, props, ctx)` | Yes | Returns the frame's SVG, as a string that starts with `<svg`. Use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element. |
68	| `meta` | No | Describes the graphic. Without it, it's `{}`. |
69	| `schema` | No | Declares the properties. Without it, it's `{}`. |
70	
71	`frame` is a whole number, counted from the graphic's first frame. A new clip starts at frame 0. Trim its front, or split it, and the later clip starts at a later frame, so the graphic carries on instead of restarting.
72	
73	`props` holds the clip's property values, and `ctx` says where the frame falls.
74	
75	The module is the only source of code. `svg`, `interpolate`, `escapeXml` and the rest of the standard library are already global, so there's nothing to import. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
76	
77	## `meta`
78	
79	Every key is optional.
80	
81	| Key | What it does |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `name` | The title shown in the inspector and the Insert Graphic sheet. Without it, the sheet makes a title from the file name. |
84	| `durationInFrames` | The length of a new clip. Without it, a new clip is 5 seconds. |
85	| `width`, `height` | The size it draws at instead of the canvas, a whole number from 1 to 8192. Insert, `add_graphic_clip`, `render_graphic` and `export_graphic` all read them. |
86	| `category` | The list it's filed under in the Insert Graphic sheet. Absent or blank means **Other**. A module in your project is listed under **This Project** whatever this says. |
87	| `description` | One line shown under the sheet's preview. |
88	
89	A `durationInFrames`, `width` or `height` that isn't a whole number in range stops the graphic being placed, and the message names the key.
90	
91	## `ctx`
92	
93	`render` receives `ctx` on every frame.
94	
95	| Key | What it is |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| `fps` | The project's frame rate, for example `30` or `29.97002997` |
98	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
99	| `durationInFrames` | The graphic's length in frames. That's the clip's length plus anything trimmed from its front, unless the [Timeline section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) sets its own. |
100	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, held between 0 and 1. A clip that runs past the graphic's length stays at 1. |
101	| `width`, `height` | The graphic's size in pixels |
102	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas, inside a nest too |
103	
104	## Resolution-independent drawing
105	
106	Write every coordinate against `ctx.width` and `ctx.height`, and one graphic draws at any size or shape.
107	
108	A unit based on the short side is the safest way to size things:
109	
110	```js
111	const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
112	```
113	
114	On a landscape canvas that's the same as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a portrait canvas drawing 1.78 times too big. See [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/).
115	
116	## The schema
117	
118	The schema declares a module's properties. Each entry becomes a row in the [Properties section](/graphics/properties/) and a value in `props`.
119	
120	| Rule | Limit |
121	| --- | --- |
122	| Keys in a schema | At most 64 |
123	| A key's spelling | Letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters |
124	| Required in every entry | A `type`, and a `default` of that type |
125	| Optional in every entry | `label` (the row's name, else the key), `help` (its tooltip), and `animate: false` |
126	
127	`animate: false` means an action never animates that property. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
128	
129	A schema that breaks a rule doesn't compile, and the error says which rule. For example, `schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`.
130	
131	## Prop types
132	
133	| `type` | Value | Extra keys | Row in the inspector |
134	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
135	| `string` | Text, at most 4,096 characters | `multiline: true` | A one-line field, or a text area with `multiline` |
136	| `number` | A finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` | A slider with a value when it has both `min` and `max`, otherwise a value field |
137	| `boolean` | `true` or `false` | | A checkbox |
138	| `color` | A CSS colour string | | A colour control |
139	| `enum` | One of its `options` | `options`, 1 to 32 strings | A pop-up |
140	| `asset` | A file name in `graphics/assets/`, or `null` or `""` for no image | `kind: "image"`, which is optional | A pop-up listing the project's pictures, with **None** first |
141	
142	- **`number`.** A `step` under 1 shows two decimal places, and a `step` of 1 or more shows whole numbers. With no `step`, two places show only when the default, `min` or `max` has a fraction.
143	- **`color`.** Write it as `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"` or a name such as `"tomato"`. A default that isn't a colour doesn't compile. `props` receives the default as you wrote it, not normalised.
144	- **`asset`.** A value of `""` stored on a clip reaches `render` as `null`, but a `default` of `""` reaches it as `""`, so test for an empty value before drawing. Pass a name to [`asset()`](/graphics/module-api/) to draw it.
145	
146	## Tolerant props
147	
148	`props` always has every key in the schema, so `render` never has to check for a missing one.
149	
150	A stored value replaces the default only when it fits the type. This matters when you change a schema after clips already hold values. A value that doesn't fit is a warning, not a failure: the default is drawn and the frame still draws. For example:
151	
152	```text
153	props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used
154	```
155	
156	A stored value whose key the schema no longer has is passed through to `render`, with a warning. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/#stale-values) for how those leftover values show in the inspector.
157	
158	## The SVG the engine draws
159	
160	Frame Job draws the string `render` returns with resvg, an SVG renderer. It draws text with the fonts graphics can use, images in PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and SVG, and compressed SVGZ images. Gradients are dithered so that dark ones don't band.
161	
162	An image must come from `graphics/assets/`, through `asset(name)`. See [Fonts and pictures in graphics](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/).
163	
164	These don't stop the frame. They're warnings, and the frame draws without the part they name:
165	
166	| Warning | What to do |
167	| --- | --- |
168	| `<image> href "x" is not an asset; the assets are: …` | Use `asset(name)` with one of the names listed. |
169	| `<image> data: URLs are not supported; put the file in graphics/assets/ and use asset(name)` | Add the file and refer to it by name. |
170	| `asset "x" is not a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG(Z) image` | Replace the file with a picture. |
171	| `font-family "x" is not in the font set; the set has: …` | Use a family it lists, or add the font. |
172	
173	A size mismatch warns too, but the picture still draws: `the SVG is 100×100 but the graphic is 1920×1080`. Using `svg(ctx, body)` for the root element avoids it.
174	
175	SVG that can't be read at all is an error, and starts `the SVG did not parse:`.
176	
177	## The sandbox
178	
179	A module runs in a sandbox, shut off from everything else on your Mac. A graphic can only use its `frame`, `props`, `ctx`, fonts and pictures, so the same frame with the same properties always draws the same pixels. These stop with an error:
180	
181	| In your module | The error |
182	| --- | --- |
183	| `Math.random()` | `Error: Math.random is not available; use random(seed)` |
184	| `import x from "x"` | `ReferenceError: Error resolving module 'x' from 'lower-third': imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global` |
185	| `new Function("…")` | `Error: Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code` |
186	| `eval("…")` | `ReferenceError: eval is not defined` |
187	
188	There's also no `fetch`, no file access, no clock, no `performance`, no `WebAssembly` and no `Intl`. For numbers with thousands separators, use `formatNumber`.
189	
190	`Date` is frozen. `Date.now()` is always `946684800000`, and `new Date()` is always 1 January 2000 at 00:00 UTC. See [Graphics in exports](/graphics/graphics-in-exports/).
191	
192	## Modern JavaScript
193	
194	Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`, `**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll` and `findLast`.
195	
196	## The time budget
197	
198	A runaway graphic reports an error instead of hanging Frame Job, because every call has a deadline.
199	
200	| Where | Budget |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| Each frame in the preview | 250 ms |
203	| Each frame in an export | 2 s |
204	| The module's top level (the code outside `render`), when it compiles | 250 ms |
205	
206	Over the budget, you get an error such as:
207	
208	```text
209	over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError: interrupted)
210	```
211	
212	When that error gives a line and column, they're where the function begins, not the statement that ran long.
213	
214	## Limits
215	
216	Each module runs in an engine of its own, with these limits:
217	
218	| Limit | Amount | Past it |
219	| --- | --- | --- |
220	| Heap | 64 MiB | An error with a line and column |
221	| Stack | 1 MiB | An error with a line and column |
222	| A graphic's side | 8192 pixels | Frame Job won't draw it |
223	| The SVG `render` returns | 8 MiB (8,388,608 bytes) | `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most 8388608 bytes` |
224	
225	`render` must return a string that starts with `<svg`. Anything else is an error:
226	
227	| What happened | The error |
228	| --- | --- |
229	| No `return` | ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?`` |
230	| A string that isn't SVG | `render returned a string that does not start with <svg at frame 12: …` |
231	| No `render` exported | ``the module exports no `render` function`` |
232	
233	A frame that fails draws a red error card on the clip. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for where errors and warnings show.

78	## How long a template runs
79	
80	The default length is in frames at your canvas's frame rate, so a 150-frame template is 5 seconds in a 30 fps project and 2.5 seconds in a 60 fps one.
81	
82	To change how long a graphic runs, drag the clip's end on the timeline. [**Follow Clip**](/graphics/size-and-timing/#follow-clip) is on for a new clip, so the exit moves with the clip's end and the entrance still plays from the first frame. A few templates also time something else by the clip's length:
83	
84	| Template | What follows the clip's length |
85	| --- | --- |
86	| Counter | Reaches its final number about 70 % of the way through. |
87	| Progress bar | Reaches its value about 60 % of the way through. |
88	| Subscribe button | The first click lands 40 % of the way through. |
89	
90	[Countdown](#countdown) and [News ticker](#news-ticker) run in real time whatever the clip's length. To fix a graphic's length so it no longer follows the clip, see [The graphic's own timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/#the-graphics-own-timeline).

186	### Arrow highlight
187	
188	Points at something on a screen recording: a rounded box drawn on around a spot, an arrow growing toward it from the side nearer the frame's centre, and a label at the arrow's tail.

190	| Property | What it does | Default |
191	| --- | --- | --- |
192	| **x**, **y** | The spot, as a fraction of the frame's width and height, 0 to 1. | 0.62, 0.42 |
193	| **boxWidth**, **boxHeight** | The box's size, as a fraction of the frame, 0.02 to 0.8. | 0.22, 0.14 |
194	| **shape** | `box+arrow`, `box` or `arrow`. | `box+arrow` |
195	| **label** | The text. Leave it empty for none. | Look here |
196	| **accent** | The box and the arrow. | `#ffd60a` |

324	
325	The three charts read their data from text fields, with entries separated by commas:
326	
327	- Values and labels pair up by position, and a value with no label has a blank one.
328	- An entry that isn't a number is dropped, so the values after it line up one label earlier.
329	- An empty entry, such as a comma at the end, counts as 0.

338	| **labels** | The labels, separated by commas. | Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat |

345	
346	A timer counting down or up, one step a second, inside a ring that empties or fills. The digits pulse on each tick, and the circle flashes in the accent colour at the end.
347

349	| --- | --- | --- |
350	| **from** | The starting number, in seconds. | 10 |
351	| **to** | The final number. Make it greater than **from** to count up. | 0 |
352	| **format** | `seconds` shows 90, `m:ss` shows 1:30 and `h:mm:ss` shows 0:01:30. | `m:ss` |
353	| **label** | The line above the digits, drawn in capitals. | Starting in |

At 60 fps that clip is 5.5 seconds, so lengthen it. For any longer count, lengthen the clip to the count plus a second.

382	| **labels** | The labels, separated by commas. | Video, Audio, Graphics, Other |
383	| **title** | The line at the top. | Where the time goes |
384	| **accent** | The first slice. | `#ff5a36` |
385	
386	The other slices take colours from a fixed set of six, in order, repeating after the sixth. The shares are rounded to whole percentages, so they may not add up to exactly 100. The card's colour isn't a property.
387	
388	### Gauge
389	
390	A 270° dial with ticks, whose accent arc and needle swing to a value while the figure counts up.
391	
392	| Property | What it does | Default |
393	| --- | --- | --- |
394	| **value** | The reading, held between **min** and **max**. | 72 |
395	| **min** | The start of the dial. | 0 |
396	| **max** | The end of the dial. At or below **min** it's taken as **min** plus 1. | 100 |
397	| **label** | The line inside the dial, drawn in capitals. | Speed |
398	| **units** | The line under the figure. | km/h |
399	| **accent** | The arc and the needle. | `#ff5a36` |
400	
401	A whole **value** counts in whole numbers, and any other shows one decimal place.
402	
403	### Line chart
404	
405	A line drawn on through its points on a dark card, a dot popping at each one, with the last value called out in a pill.
406	
407	| Property | What it does | Default |
408	| --- | --- | --- |
409	| **values** | The points, separated by commas. | 12, 18, 15, 26, 22, 34, 41 |
410	| **labels** | The labels along the bottom, separated by commas. | Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul |
411	| **title** | The line at the top. | Monthly active users |
412	| **area** | Shades the area under the line. | On |
413	| **accent** | The line, the dots' outlines, the shading and the pill. | `#2d7ff9` |
414	
415	The scale runs from 0, or from the lowest value if that's negative, up to the highest. A single value draws one dot and no line. The card's colour isn't a property.
416	
417	### Progress bar
418	
419	A labelled bar on a dark plate, filling to a percentage with the figure counting, and a shine sweeping across it once it has filled.
420	
421	| Property | What it does | Default |
422	| --- | --- | --- |
423	| **value** | How far it fills, 0 to 100. | 68 |
424	| **label** | The text above the bar. | Rendering |
425	| **showPercent** | Shows the percentage at the right. | On |
426	| **position** | `bottom`, `center` or `top`. | `bottom` |
427	| **accent** | The fill. | `#2d7ff9` |
428	
429	## Any canvas shape
430	
431	Templates size themselves by the shorter side of the canvas, so nothing grows too large on a tall project.
432	
433	Seventeen of them are laid out for all three shapes. Everything they draw stays inside the title-safe area, the frame less 5 % on every side, at 1920 × 1080, 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080. Their entrances are a spring, a wipe or a fade, and never a move in from outside the frame. Long text is fitted or wrapped to stay inside, down to a smallest size for each text, so a paragraph typed where a title belongs can still run over.
434	
435	The other six are Bar chart, Callout, Counter, Kinetic type, Lower third and Title card. They don't keep to the title-safe area, and a left-aligned Lower third enters from beyond the frame's left edge. Once settled, with their default text, their words sit at least 24 pixels inside a 1080 × 1920 frame. Only Title card fits its title and Kinetic type wraps its text, so check your own words on a tall canvas. [Safe areas](/canvas/safe-areas/) shows the title-safe guide in the preview.
436	
437	A square canvas takes the landscape layout.
438	
439	## Templates end clean
440	
441	The same seventeen each have an accent colour and leave in about their last 15 frames, so the last frame is bare. An overlay ends clear, and a card ends on its background alone. A card's background never animates: only what's on it moves or fades.
442	
443	The other six end their own way:
444	
445	| Template | At the end of the clip |
446	| --- | --- |
447	| Lower third | Fades out over the last 15 frames and ends clear. |
448	| Title card | Its text fades over the last 18 frames, leaving the gradient. |
449	| Bar chart, Callout, Counter, Kinetic type | Hold to the last frame and stop with the clip. |
450	
451	## Template fonts and glyphs
452	
453	Templates draw only with fonts that come with Frame Job, so a project looks the same on any Mac. The font isn't a property. To change it, [edit the graphic's code](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
454	
455	| Used for | Font |
456	| --- | --- |
457	| Text in most templates | Montserrat, extra bold or black |
458	| Digits that tick, the shares in Donut chart's legend, Counter's label and the figures in Bar chart | IBM Plex Mono |
459	| Window frame's title and address | Source Sans 3, semibold |
460	| Title card's title | Anton |
461	| Title card's kicker and Bar chart's labels | Bebas Neue |
462	| Callout's label | Darker Grotesque |
463	
464	Every symbol is a generic shape drawn by the template, never a brand's artwork: the keycap symbols, the heart, the bell, the play triangle and the glyphs in Handle tag. None of them is a platform's own logo.
465	
466	## Good to know
467	
468	- Each insert copies the template into the project under a name not yet in use, such as `lower-third`, then `lower-third-2`. Undo takes the clip away, and the copy stays until you [delete it](/graphics/manage-graphics/).
469	- Your copy is yours to change, and it stays as it was when you inserted it. [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) covers the one exception.
470	- Most properties can [change over time with an action](/graphics/animate-properties/). These keep one value for the whole clip: **number** in Chapter card and Step badge, **values** and **labels** in Donut chart and Line chart, **keys** in Keyboard keys, **items** in News ticker and **count** in Social popup.
471	
472	## With an agent
473	
474	`list_graphics` lists the templates by category, as the sheet does. `insert_graphic` places one at the playhead: give it the name `list_graphics` shows, such as `arrow-highlight`, with `from` set to `template`. The reply names the project's copy, which may be `arrow-highlight-2`. To fill in the properties afterwards, use `set_graphic`, with the names in the tables above. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/).
475

11	<AtAGlance

15	
16	A graphic's code is a **module**, the file `graphics/<name>.js` inside the project, and `name` in these tools is that file's name without `.js`. Fonts, pictures, renames, deletes and packages are on [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

20	## Write, place, change and check
21	
22	A graphic made by an agent usually goes through these steps.
23	
24	<Steps>
25	
26	1. Read the API once with [`graphic_reference`](#graphic_reference).
27	
28	2. Write the module with [`write_graphic`](#write_graphic). It returns the result of compiling that exact text. If it failed, fix the source and write it again.
29	
30	3. Look at it with [`render_graphic`](#render_graphic), which draws frames with no clip on the timeline.
31	
32	4. Place it with [`add_graphic_clip`](#add_graphic_clip), giving the track, the time and any values it should draw with. [`insert_graphic`](#insert_graphic) places a graphic at the playhead instead, as the Insert Graphic sheet does.
33	
34	5. Change it with [`set_graphic`](#set_graphic). To animate a property, add an action with `add_action` and say what the property ends at with `set_action_end`. See [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).
35	
36	6. Check a frame of the finished timeline with [`render_frame`](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/#render_frame).
37	
38	</Steps>

40	## `graphic_reference`
41	
42	Returns the whole graphics API as Markdown, for a model to read once before it writes a graphic. It covers a module's shape, `ctx`, the schema's types, the standard library, fonts, the sandbox, the limits and worked examples.
43	
44	It's the same file as **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).
45	
46	It takes no argument of its own, and it's the one tool on this page that needs no project open. A `project`, when given, must still name an open one.
47	
48	## `write_graphic`
49	
50	Writes a module's JavaScript into the project, compiles it and returns the result for that text. The folder `graphics/` is made if it isn't there yet. A person does the same by saving the file in an editor. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/).
51	
52	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
53	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
54	| `name` | string | Yes | The module's name: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, starting with a letter or a digit, at most 63 characters. |
55	| `source` | string | Yes | The whole module's JavaScript. It exports `render`, and optionally `meta` and `schema`. |
56	
57	It returns:
58	
59	| Key | What it holds |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| `name`, `path`, `revision` | The module, its file, and the SHA-256 of its text. |
62	| `ok` | Whether the text compiled. |
63	| `meta`, `schema` | What the module declares. Both are empty when `ok` is false. |
64	| `diagnostics` | A list of `{level, message, line, column, frame}`. With `ok` false, they say where it went wrong. With `ok` true, they're the module's top-level warnings, such as `asset()` used outside `render`. |
65	| `clips` | The ids of the clips drawn by this module. They redraw with the new text at once. |
66	| `kept` | The revisions of the module's kept earlier texts, newest first. |
67	
68	A module that doesn't compile isn't an error. The call succeeds with `ok` false, and the file stays in the folder as written, so fix the source and write it again. The call itself fails for a name that isn't a module name, or a file that can't be written.
69	
70	A write can't be undone and doesn't mark the project edited, but the text it replaced is kept, up to the last 10 for each module. [`restore_graphic`](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/#restore_graphic) brings one back.
71	
72	## `get_graphic`
73	
74	Reads one module, or the whole graphics folder. The module's half is what the [**Source** section](/graphics/graphic-tab/#source) of the Graphic sub-tab shows a person.
75	
76	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
77	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
78	| `name` | string | No | The module to read. Leave it out to read the folder. |
79	
80	With `name`, it returns `name`, `source`, `path`, `revision`, `ok`, `meta`, `schema`, `diagnostics`, `clips` and `kept`, with the same meanings as [`write_graphic`](#write_graphic). A name the folder doesn't hold gives an error that lists what it does hold.
81	
82	Without `name`, it returns:
83	
84	| Key | What it holds |
85	| --- | --- |
86	| `folder` | The folder's full path. It's given even before the folder exists. |
87	| `folder_exists` | False until the first write makes the folder. |
88	| `modules` | Every module, as `{name, revision, ok, clips}`. |
89	| `families` | The font families the project's graphics can draw with. |
90	| `assets` | The pictures in `graphics/assets/`. |
91	| `warnings` | What Frame Job skipped or couldn't watch when it read the folder, in plain sentences. |
92	| `history` | `{name, kept}` for every name with kept texts, deleted modules included. |
93	
94	A module saved a moment ago from outside can read `ok` false with one diagnostic saying the app hasn't compiled it yet. Call again.
95	
96	## `render_graphic`
97	
98	Draws a module without a clip, to look at it before placing it. There's no control for this in the app, because a person looks at the preview instead.
99	
100	### Render graphic options
101	
102	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
103	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
104	| `name` | string | Yes | The module to draw. |
105	| `frames` | array of integers | No | The frames to draw, 1 to 16 of them, in the order given. Not with `frame`. |
106	| `frame` | integer | No | One frame to draw, 0 or more. Not with `frames`. With neither, frame 0 is drawn. |
107	| `props` | object | No | The values to draw with, keyed by the schema's names. A key left out draws with the schema's default. |
108	| `width` | integer | No | The width to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.width`, else the canvas. |
109	| `height` | integer | No | The height to draw at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.height`, else the canvas. |
110	| `format` | string | No | `png` (the default) for a contact sheet, or `svg` for one frame's text. |
111	| `max_width` | integer | No | The widest the sheet may be, 64 to 8192 pixels. The default is 2048. 8192 keeps a 1920-wide graphic's two cells at full size. |
112	| `background` | string | No | What the sheet is painted on: `transparent` (the default), `checker`, or a hex colour as `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`, in either case. |
113	| `path` | string | No | Where to write the sheet. It's always a `.png`, and its folder must exist. Leave it out for a temporary file. |
114	
115	`max_width`, `background` and `path` belong to the sheet, and `svg` won't take them.
116	
117	Each frame is drawn as a clip would draw it. The frame rate is the canvas's, `durationInFrames` is the module's `meta` value or else 5 seconds, and a frame at or past that length is still drawn, with `progress` at 1, as a longer clip draws it.
118	
119	### The contact sheet
120	
121	The `png` format returns an image the model can see, a text block, and a file on disk. The frames sit on a near-square grid, top left first, and each frame's number is printed in a dark strip under its cell. Sixteen frames make a 4 by 4 grid.
122	
123	- Only the cells scale down to fit `max_width`, never the 8-pixel gaps or the 24-pixel labels. Cells are never scaled up, and the sheet is never more than 8192 pixels tall.
124	- `checker` paints 16-pixel grey squares, which shows up a graphic's transparent areas.
125	- A frame that fails draws its error card in its cell. The sheet still comes back, and the text adds a sentence with the error and where it is. A frame that only warned adds a sentence too.
126	- The text says the frames, each cell's size and scale, the grid, the sheet's size and the background, and ends "Written to `<path>`."
127	
128	A sheet draws at most 134,217,728 pixels of frames, counted as frames × width × height. That's two frames at 8192 × 8192, or sixteen at 3840 × 2160. Past that the call fails before any frame is drawn, so ask for fewer frames or a smaller size.
129	
130	### One frame as SVG
131	
132	With `format: "svg"`, it returns `name`, `frame`, `ok`, `svg` (the frame's SVG text), `diagnostics`, and `ctx`, the values the frame was drawn with: `fps`, `time`, `durationInFrames`, `progress`, `width`, `height` and `canvas`.
133	
134	It draws one frame and writes no file. A frame that fails isn't an error here either: `ok` is false, `svg` is null and `diagnostics` say why.
135	
136	### When it won't run
137	
138	`render_graphic` won't run when:
139	
140	- The module isn't in the folder, or doesn't compile. The error lists what the folder holds, or gives the first compile error.
141	- Both `frame` and `frames` are given, or `frames` doesn't hold 1 to 16 whole numbers of 0 or more.
142	- `format` is `svg` with more than one frame, or with `path`, `background` or `max_width`.
143	- `max_width`, `width`, `height` or `background` is out of range, or the folder of `path` doesn't exist.
144	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range. The error names the key.
145	
146	## `list_graphics`
147	
148	Lists the graphics **Insert ▸ Graphic…** offers, in the sheet's order. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
149	
150	It takes no argument of its own. It returns `categories`, a list of `{name, graphics}`, and each graphic is:
151	
152	| Key | What it holds |
153	| --- | --- |
154	| `name` | What [`insert_graphic`](#insert_graphic) takes. |
155	| `title` | The module's `meta.name`, else its name made into a title. Two **This Project** graphics with one title show as "title — name". |
156	| `description` | The module's `meta.description`, or null. |
157	| `category` | The module's own category. |
158	| `from` | `template` or `project`, which is what `insert_graphic` takes as `from`. |
159	| `ok` | False for a module that doesn't compile. It's still listed. |
160	
161	**This Project** comes first when the project's `graphics/` holds a module, and lists every module there, whatever its own category. The bundled templates follow by category, A to Z, each module's `meta.category` or else **Other**, which is always last. Within a category, graphics sort by title.
162	
163	## `insert_graphic`
164	
165	Places a graphic at the playhead, as the **Insert** button in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** does. See [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).
166	
167	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
168	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
169	| `name` | string | Yes | The graphic's name as `list_graphics` gives it. |
170	| `from` | string | Yes | `template` for one of the bundled templates, `project` for a module already in the project's `graphics/`. |
171	
172	The clip goes on the front track when it fits there, otherwise on a new track above everything, at the module's `meta` length and size. It's one undo step, **Insert Graphic**. With a nest open, it lands inside the nest.
173	
174	A template is first copied into `graphics/` under a free name such as `lower-third` or `lower-third-2`. That copy can't be undone, so undoing the insert takes the clip away and leaves the module. A project module is placed as it is, with no copy.
175	
176	It returns what [any edit returns](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/), and `name` says which module the clip is drawn by.
177	
178	It won't place anything when:
179	
180	- `name` isn't a template or a module of the project. The error lists what there is.
181	- The module doesn't compile. The error gives the first problem, and a template's copy stays in `graphics/`.
182	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range.
183	
184	## `add_graphic_clip`
185	
186	Places a clip drawn by a module already in `graphics/`, on a track and at a time you choose. Use it when you need more say than `insert_graphic` gives. **Insert ▸ Graphic…** is a template's write followed by this. See [Place a clip](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#place-a-clip).
187	
188	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
189	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
190	| `track` | integer | Yes | The track's id. `get_project` lists them. |
191	| `at` | integer | Yes | The start, in ticks. |
192	| `name` | string | Yes | The module. |
193	| `duration` | integer | No | The length, in ticks, at least one frame. Default: the module's `meta.durationInFrames` at the canvas's rate, else 5 seconds. |
194	| `width` | integer | No | The width the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.width`, else the canvas. |
195	| `height` | integer | No | The height the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. Default: `meta.height`, else the canvas. |
196	| `props` | object | No | The values to draw with, keyed by the schema's names, at most 64. A key left out draws with the schema's default. |
197	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to add the clip inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
198	
199	Like a shape, the clip has no source of its own. Use [`set_graphic`](#set_graphic) to change what it's drawn from, and `set_video` to place it in the picture.
200	
201	Each key of `props` is checked against the module's schema as the file reads now. A key the schema lacks, a wrong type or a value out of range gives an error naming its dotted path. A colour is stored as lowercase hex, and a null is dropped.
202	
203	It returns what any edit returns, with the new clip in `new_clips`, and it's one undo step, **Add Graphic**.
204	
205	It won't place the clip when:
206	
207	- The module isn't in the folder, or doesn't compile. The error lists what the folder holds, or gives the first compile error.
208	- A `meta` value it would use isn't a whole number in range.
209	- The canvas is wider or taller than 8192 pixels and no size was given.
210	- The clip would overlap another one on the track, as for any clip.
211	
212	## `set_graphic`
213	
214	Changes what graphic clips are drawn from: the module, the size, the graphic's own length and its properties. It's the same as editing **Properties**, **Size** and **Timeline** in the [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) and [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).
215	
216	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
217	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
218	| `clips` | array of integers | Yes | The clip ids, at least one. |
219	| `patch` | object | Yes | The keys to change, below. |
220	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to edit inside that nest. |
221	
222	| Patch key | What it does |
223	| --- | --- |
224	| `name` | Draws the clips from another module, which must be in the folder and compile. |
225	| `width`, `height` | The size the module draws at, 1 to 8192 pixels. |
226	| `length` | The graphic's own timeline, in ticks. It snaps to a frame and is at least one frame. Null ends it with the clip, which is **Follow Clip**. |
227	| `props` | The base values, merged key by key, at most 64 on a clip. A null removes its key. |
228	
229	A null for a property that an action on the clip animates doesn't remove it. It sets the schema's default, so the animation keeps its start. To animate a property, use `add_action` and then `set_action_end`.
230	
231	A patch with `props` or `name` is checked against a schema: the one of the module the patch names, otherwise the one module every clip is drawn by.
232	
233	It returns what any edit returns, and it's one undo step, **Graphic Properties**. A patch that changes nothing makes no undo step, and that includes a colour re-sent in another spelling.
234	
235	It won't run when:
236	
237	- One of the clips isn't a graphic. Nothing changes on the others either.
238	- `props` is sent with no `name` to clips drawn by two different modules. Set them one module at a time.
239	- The patch has `in`, which only trims and splits can change, or any other key it doesn't know.
240	- A value fails its check. The error names it, and a property by its dotted path.
241	
242	## Editing the folder with your own file tools
243	
244	An agent can also edit the graphics folder directly, and Frame Job sees a change within a moment. Ask `get_graphic` with no `name` for the folder's path.
245	
246	| What | Where |
247	| --- | --- |
248	| Modules | `<name>.js` |
249	| Fonts | `fonts/`, as `.ttf` or `.otf` |
250	| Pictures | `assets/` |
251	
252	`history/`, `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are Frame Job's own, so leave them alone. `history/` holds the kept texts that `restore_graphic` reads, and `API.md` and `API.d.ts` are the reference.
253	
254	A module's text is kept when Frame Job sees it replaced while the project is open, and that includes a save from an outside editor. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for how changes are picked up.
